c.tagline: A laid-back Sinai backpacker town famous for the Blue Hole dive site and cheap beachfront cafes
langs: English (widely spoken due to backpacker/diving tourism)

card: Accepted at larger dive centers and hotels; cash preferred at beachfront cafes and markets

taxi.fareNote: Dahab is small enough to walk or bike between most areas; taxis mainly used for airport transfers or desert excursions

emergency.note: Tourist police (180) can assist with English-language support

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Central Dahab (Masbat and Mashraba) is very walkable along the beachfront promenade; the Blue Hole and Canyon require a short taxi ride

safety.safety: Generally safe and relaxed, popular with solo travelers and long-term digital nomads; check current travel advisories for the wider Sinai region
safety.crime: Very low crime; diving safety (especially at the Blue Hole) is the main practical caution

hood_landmark.Masbat / Asalah: Masbat's beachfront promenade of cafes and dive shops
hood_landmark.Mashraba: Mashraba's central restaurant and shopping strip
hood_landmark.The Blue Hole: The famous Blue Hole dive site north of town
hood_landmark.The Lagoon: The Lagoon's windsurfing and kitesurfing school area

avoid.reason: Avoid overland travel into the North and interior Sinai away from the main coastal road, which most governments advise against due to security risks.
Vendor hassle is mild by Egyptian standards, but vet dive and quad-bike operators carefully and refuse any drug offers — penalties are severe.

hood_desc: The bohemian northern beachfront strip of cushion-seated cafes, dive centers, and budget guesthouses, the heart of Dahab's backpacker scene.
The central strip with the highest concentration of restaurants, shops, and mid-range hotels.
A quieter, more residential area to the south, popular for longer stays away from the tourist bustle.
A world-famous (and genuinely hazardous for untrained divers) sinkhole dive site a short drive north of town.
A shallow lagoon south of town that's one of the world's top windsurfing and kitesurfing destinations.

water.note: Tap water is desalinated and brackish; drink bottled water.

transit.sys: No formal municipal transit; walking, bikes, and taxis cover the compact town
transit.map: Not applicable; the town is small and easily walkable
transit.note: Most excursions (Blue Hole, Canyon, Mount Sinai) are arranged through dive centers or hotels

transport.air: Sharm El Sheikh International Airport (SSH), about 1-1.5 hr away, is the nearest major airport
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Dahab
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Cairo, Sharm El Sheikh, and Nuweiba
transport.car: Rental cars available; taxis and shared minibuses are the more common way to arrive from Sharm El Sheikh

airport.name: Sharm El Sheikh International Airport (nearest major gateway)
airport.transport: Taxi, shared minibus, or hotel transfer

net.w: Free wifi standard in cafes and guesthouses
net.ops: Vodafone Egypt, Orange Egypt, Etisalat Misr
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in cafes, popular with digital nomads
net.ap: A Vodafone or Orange Egypt tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: 10-15% is customary for dive guides and instructors
